text: {"frames":["A smell of wet wool and hot waffles crept under the door of the fourth floor, and a map was pinned there that was not there yesterday. The map showed the canals of the Tower in green thread, and one stretch of water had been coloured in with a wet brush. Pim, the lock keeper's boy, tapped the paper and said the coloured stretch was the water that had gone missing from the mill race. That stretch is {x} of the whole map. What percentage of the map has gone missing, so the mill wheel can turn again?","Somewhere in the fog a bell began to toll, although the village under the water has been quiet for years. The sound came up through the canal like a slow breath. Bas stood on the bridge and listened to each stroke. The bell had rung {x} of the strokes it owed the night. What percentage of the night's strokes has already sounded?","\"Sh, don't wake the watchman,\" whispered Anke at the dyke. Nobody had ever seen him by day, yet every morning his lantern hung lit on the sluice gate. A crack had opened in the dyke, and a thin silver line of water ran through it. A note pinned to the gate said that {x} of the dyke has been mended. What percentage of the dyke is mended, so the water stops?","Quick, come inside, the windows of the crooked house with the hoist beam are all glowing. Nobody is in the house, but the kettle on the stove is still warm. On the table lies a tulip bulb box with a label that says {x} of the bulbs have sprouted in the cellar. The lamps will only go dark once the cellar count is right. What percentage of the bulbs has sprouted?","Quick, come up, the clock on the Tower has struck an hour that does not exist. The hands sit between the twelve and the thirteen, and a little bell hums inside the case. Lot, the clock mender, holds a wooden gear with a row of teeth. Only {x} of the teeth are still left, and the clock can run again only when the gap is known. What percentage of the teeth is still there?"]}
